description.narrative:
Statistics on international migration between African countries and out of Africa are compiled by the African Union Commission, STATAFRIC, the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the International Labour Organisation (ILO), the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), Regional Economic Communities (RECs) and by government and private national institutions. Although some improvements have taken place in the last years, migration statistics in Africa generally suffers from poor quality, poorly aligned data collection periods, unharmonised definitions and standards, lacking possibilities to use administrative data sources and a low level of cooperation and data sharing between national data producers.
Quality statistics on migration, mobility and displacement are fundamental to the implementation of adequate policies on migration at national, regional, and continental level. Yet, in many countries, even the most general statistics on migration are incomplete, out-of-date or do not exist. Improvement in this area requires knowledge of the principles of collecting, compiling and analyzing migration statistics. Likewise, policymakers and other users need to be aware of the definitions and measurement issues related to the data to be able to interpret them.
The Migration Statistics II project contributes to improving the availability of relevant and good quality statistics on migration in Africa for use in decision- and policymaking on migration issues.
The second phase of Migration Statistics II relies on the significant work done in Capacity Development in Migration Statistics which was implemented over the period January 2019- December 2022.

Statistik om migration mellan afrikanska länder och ut ur Afrika sammanställs av Afrikanska Unionens institut för statistik, STATAFRIC, samt av FN:s Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), International Labour Organisation (ILO), International Organisation for Migration (IOM), Regional Economic Communities (RECs) och av statliga och privata nationella institutioner. Även om vissa förbättringar har skett under de senaste åren lider migrationsstatistiken i Afrika i allmänhet av dålig kvalitet, bristfälligt koordinerade insamlingsperioder, oharmoniserade definitioner och standarder, bristande möjligheter att använda administrativa datakällor och en låg nivå av samarbete och datadelning mellan nationella dataproducenter. Kvalitetsstatistik om migration och rörlighet är grundläggande för genomförandet av adekvata migrationsstrategier på nationell, regional och kontinental nivå men i många länder är även den mest grundläggande statistiken om migration ofullständig, inaktuell eller existerar inte. Förbättringar på detta område kräver kunskap om principerna för insamling, sammanställning och analys av migrationsstatistik. Likaså måste beslutsfattare och andra användare vara medvetna om definitionerna och mätproblem relaterade till data för att kunna tolka densamma. Projektet Migration Statistics II bidrar till att förbättra tillgången till relevant statistik av god kvalitet om migration i Afrika för användning i policyutformning och beslutsfattande avseende migration.
Den andra fasen av programmet bygger på det betydande arbete som gjorts genomförts under programmets första fas, Capacity Development in Migration Statistics, som implementerades under perioden januari 2019–december 2022.

The project objective is increased availability of high-quality migration statistics to users enabling adequate management of the effects of migration on women and men, girls and boys. In addition, the migration statistics will be used to monitor and evaluate the continental and international agendas such as Agenda 2063, Agenda 2030 and Global Compact on Migration.
The project will strengthen the capacity of STATAFRIC, RECs and Member States to produce, harmonize and disseminate migration statistics. This will be achieved through the implementation of capacity development activities leading to tangible results. Thus, five components have been identified (with the first four from the first phase of the project) completed by a new fifth component:
Component 1: Statistics production
Component 2: Concepts and methods
Component 3: Dissemination and publication
Component 4: Coordination
Component 5: Forced displacement
The project will consolidate the results obtained during the first phase of Capacity Development for Migration Statistics and to support STATAFRIC and the selected RECs in the implementation of continental and regional statistical plans. The project will be funded by Sida and the Norwegian Development Cooperation Agency (Norad) who will contribute to the project with SEK 25 925 000. Norad who will cover the cost for one Long Term Advisor, two statistical officers located in the RECs, and (yearly) 15 weeks of short-term missions, support for regional workshops, two study tours to Norway, and 10 weeks of remote support. Norad will also cover the cost for project coordination at Statistics Norway.

Several notable results have been achieved over the reporting period, reflecting both planned outcomes and adaptive responses to emerging challenges:
1. In June, Sida approved an amendment to the Migration Statistics II agreement with Statistics Sweden, which included an additional allocation of SEK 21 million. The funding was provided to address a financial shortfall resulting from Norways shift in priorities.
2. In response to concerns raised by the previous Programme Manager, Sida HQ is reviewing the interpretation of the Service Purchase Arrangement concerning fixed assets. The response is still pending.
3. Sida approved the recruitment of an IT officer for STATAFRIC. This decision aligns with the World Banks support for a social and population statistics officer, ensuring coordination and avoiding duplication of efforts. It also supports the ambition to make migration displacement data more accessible through digital solutions.
4. The project team conducted a thorough revision of the results framework, clarifying the theory of change and intervention logic with support from Niras. To better align with the new RBM framework and enable more meaningful evaluation, the Mid-Term Review was rescheduled to Q1 2026.
5. RECs, including AMU, EAC, and IGAD, initiated resource mobilization dialogues with key stakeholders, laying the foundation for sustainable financing.
Key results achieved per component:
Component outcome 1 Statistics production
Following the gender review conducted in early 2024, two key outcomes were achieved: gender-disaggregated data is now a mandatory component of regional reporting, and a model for continuous self-assessment of gender mainstreaming was developed and integrated into project monitoring.
STATAFRIC is on track to publish the fourth edition of the LMSRA in 2025, which will include sex-disaggregated data and a stronger gender perspective. A gender expert has also been recruited.
COMESA tailored its efforts through targeted support to NTWGs in its member states, reflecting a differentiated strategy based on national needs and COMESAs coordination model. AMU began production of its second migration report, with an emphasis on sex-disaggregated data.
The RTWG discussed which data should be collected and exchanged in the questionnaire to better align with the evolving contexts of member states. ECCAS established its RTWG and began planning for its first regional report, while ECOWAS concluded the production phase of its third regional report, incorporating enhanced gender-sensitive data analysis tools.
Component 2 Concepts and methods
STATAFRIC led the development of comprehensive guidelines on migration and forced displacement statistics, in collaboration with international and regional experts. Finalization of these guidelines is expected later this year.
The RECs engaged in harmonization efforts to align definitions and statistical tools with international norms. RTWGs played a central role in facilitating these discussions (particularly in EAC, IGAD, and ECOWAS) where shared regional tools were validated within the RTWG. ECCAS and AMU initiated regional consultations to begin this process. COMESA took a slightly different approach by prioritizing direct engagement with member states through workshops and targeted capacity development for national teams.
Component 3 Dissemination and publication
STATAFRIC refined its data compilation and analysis processes in order to publish the fourth edition of the LMSRA in 2025, which will include sex-disaggregated data and a strengthened gender perspective.
It also developed a database containing current migration data and outlined a plan for the creation of a migration data portal, both scheduled for launch in 2026. These initiatives aim to improve data accessibility for stakeholders.
Although no regional reports were published in 2024, several are currently in progress for publication in 2025, with increased emphasis on country ownership and participation in data validation and content production.
Component 4: Coordination
A new cooperation agreement between Statistics Sweden and the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU) has been signed, and a new LTA for migration statistics has been hired to be placed at ECOWAS.
STATAFRIC reinforced the coordination of migration statistics through the STG meetings, which saw increased participation and the formalization of a biannual schedule. These meetings contribute to sustainable coordination within the African Statistical System and support effective SHaSA2 implementation.
Several RECs (including AMU, EAC, and IGAD) have coordinated with stakeholders such as the WB, IOM, and AfDB on co-funding activities. However, these efforts have been ad hoc and conducted on a per-activity basis.
Regarding funding for regional migration experts, discussions are still in the early stages but reflect a growing recognition of the need for sustainable financing, particularly to ensure the continuation of their roles beyond project-based support.
Component 5: Forced displacement
Forced displacement statistics have been more systematically integrated into LMSRA planning and processes. A regional expert group on forced displacement was established, with STATAFRIC working closely with RECs and external stakeholders.
A key development was the study visit to Statistics Norway, which inspired IGAD to initiate a dedicated sub-group on forced displacement. Additionally, Djibouti now leads the African sub-group under the global Expert Group on Refugee and IDP Statistics (EGRISS) structure.
All RECs have begun integrating forced displacement topics into their workshops and capacity-building activities. Some, including ECCAS and ECOWAS, have made further progress in understanding and applying these concepts in practice, supported by STATAFRIC-led initiatives.
Overall, activities are progressing as expected. There have been some delays in recruitment of staff, but most positions are now filled indicating a positive trajectory toward achieving the interventions objectives. Still awaiting the recruitment of technical staff at AMU.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
